title: Designing a Tachistoscopic Split-Brain Visual Field Protocol
description: Construct an experimental protocol to test lateralized processing in surgical callosotomy patients using chimeric faces and words.
problemStatement:
You are designing a cognitive neuroscience experiment to investigate dual consciousness in a split-brain patient with complete corpus callosotomy.

### Your Mission:
1. **Tachistoscopic Parameters**: Specify display duration (e.g., 120 ms) and explain why durations >200 ms would ruin the experimental design by allowing saccadic eye movements.
2. **Chimeric Faces Test**: A stimulus combining the left half of a woman's face and the right half of a man's face is flashed at the central fixation point. Predict the patient's verbal answer vs. what the patient selects when pointing with their left hand.
3. **Cross-Cueing Prevention**: Describe two potential 'cross-cueing' strategies the patient's two hemispheres might exploit to communicate non-verbally (e.g., subtle head turns, tongue movements, or emotional facial twitches), and explain how your protocol eliminates them.
hints: Hint 1: Saccades take roughly 150-200 ms to initiate; a 100 ms flash ensures the image hits only the intended visual field.
Hint 2: The right hemisphere (pointing with left hand) recognizes faces holistically, while the left hemisphere (verbal) recognizes the right half face.
